newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stks close off as profit-taking continues.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stks close off as profit-taking continues.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off in quiet trade, but the recent bout of profit-taking on the run up in share prices over the New Year should subside in coming days, traders said.
"Stocks should rebound again from undervalued prices, tempting back foreign money," Financorp broker Hector Perez said.

The market's leading index dropped 1.17 percent to end at 6,523.89 points as 20.4 million shares traded worth 2.8 billion bolivars ($5.9 million), according to preliminary figures from the stock exchange.

Among traded issues, 32 fell, six rose and three closed flat. Traders said the market was unmoved on news telephone company CANTV had applied to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for a five-year $150 million Yankee bond. CANTV closed off 6.00 bolivars at 1964.00. "Prices are still finding their true level after December's market rally," said Interacciones broker Piero Montelli.
Among other widely-held stocks, utility Electricidad de Caracas slipped 10.95 bolivars to end at 488.05 while Mavesa lost 2.00 bolivars closing at 156.00.
